newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Jan palm oil output seen down 11 pct-Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Jan palm oil output seen down 11 pct-Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in January is estimated to have fallen by 11 percent to 568,000 tonnes from December 1996, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Tuesday. He has previously projected a fall of 9.5 pct.
Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of January at 715,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 792,687 tonnes at end-December.

Wong said in a report that the downward revision reflected mainly poorer than expected output in Peninsular Malaysia, especially in the two leading producing states of Johor and Pahang which experienced dry weather conditions during the greater part of the month.
"There was little evidence of harvesting of under-ripe fruits ahead of the the double festive holidays in early February," Wong said in his latest report.
Overall production in Peninsular Malaysia is estimated to have dropped more than 12 percent. East Malaysia fared better when its output fell around five pct

"In recent days beneficial rains with 30-60 percent coverage had been falling in most crop areas," Wong said. "This coupled with a resumption of normal operations after the festive holidays in February 7-14 should ensure a significant recovery in production in the last 10 days of this month."

He said with new export demand continuing sluggish, no significant changes in prices or market direction is likely in the next two weeks ar at least until the next Malaysia Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) release on February 22.
